chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad ibn ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

When one performs Itikaaf for a day and there is no stipulation, it is for him to go out and terminate the Itikaaf. And if he stays for two days and there is no stipulation, it is not for him to terminate his Itikaaf until three days have passed.
ai.seo_question: What are the rules for ending Itikaaf if no specific duration was initially promised?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the binding nature of Itikaaf based on duration, establishing a jurisprudential precedent where a single day remains revocable, while two days create an obligation to complete the standard three-day period. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on intentionality and the gradual commitment in acts of worship, distinguishing between voluntary flexibility and binding vows. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the conditions under which a worshipper may exit the mosque without penalty.
